extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, litigants, and judges involved in Texas public-agency bond validation and election-contest litigation (Art. 717m-1 §8)
extracted.subtask_short: posting bond for public agency validations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing when and how a Texas public agency may require an opposing party or intervenor to post a damage bond under Tex. Rev. Civ. Stat. Ann. art. 717m-1 §8, including hearing, evidence, amount-setting, appeal, and consequences for failure to post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory bond authority (Art. 717m-1, §8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The public agency may ask the court for an order that any opposing party or intervenor (except the attorney general) post a bond with sufficient surety, payable to the public agency, for the payment of all damages and costs which may accrue by reason of the delay occasioned by the continued participation of the opposing party in the proceedings if the public agency finally prevails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory provision authorizes the court to require a bond prior to final judgment and sets the basic scope (damages and costs due to delay) and beneficiary (public agency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger: failure to show entitlement to temporary injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless at the hearing the opposing party or intervenor establishes facts which, in the judgment of the court, would entitle him to a temporary injunction against the issuance of the securities, the court shall grant the motion of the public agency and fix the amount of the bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute conditions imposition of the bond on the opponent's inability to show entitlement to a preliminary (temporary) injunction — i.e., bond is required only when the opponent cannot demonstrate merit sufficient for injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's authority to fix bond amount and receive evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall fix the amount of the bond in an amount found by the court to be sufficient to cover all damages and costs which may accrue by reason of the delay; the court in its discretion may receive evidence at the hearing with respect to the amount of the damages and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible evidence to determine amount 'shall include but not be limited to anticipated increases in interest rates and in construction and financing costs.' The court may rely on expert testimony and other speculative but probative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and timing of bond hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall issue an order directed to the opposing party or intervenor, which order, together with a copy of the motion, shall be served on the opposing party or intervenor, or on his attorney of record, personally or by registered mail, requiring appearance at a time and place not sooner than 5 nor later than 10 days after entry of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions involving more than one opposing party may be heard together if the court so directs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation among multiple opposing parties
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one opposing party or intervenor is a participant in the proceedings, the court in its discretion may allocate the amount of the bond among the opposing parties or intervenors according to the extent or degree of their participation in the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court may fix the amount for a particular opposing party only if a motion as described in the section was made and granted as to that opposing party or intervenor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to post bond
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bond with sufficient surety is not filed by the opposing party or intervenor within 10 days after entry of the order fixing the amount of the bond, the opposing party or intervenor shall be dismissed by the court; the dismissal shall constitute a final judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no appeal is taken or if appeal is unsuccessful and no bond is posted within 10 days after the appropriate order, no court shall have further jurisdiction of any action to the extent it involves any issue which was or could have been raised in the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability and expedited appellate review
rubrics_metrics.description: An order of the court fixing the amount of the bond to be posted, denying the motion of a public agency, or dismissing a party for failure to file a bond may be appealed as provided in Section 9 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals under the Act are given priority over other cases (except habeas), and the courts of civil appeals and the Supreme Court must assure priority and act with the least possible delay; the appellate court may modify the lower court's order and enter the modified order as final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for speculative, prospective damages evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The calculation of prospective damages — especially based on rising interest rates — is by its nature somewhat speculative; the Act explicitly authorizes consideration of such possibility and does not require the certainty or particularity that a suit on the bond itself would require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may accept projections (e.g., likelihood that some portion of issue will be sold within a year, anticipated rise in interest rates by specified percentages, twenty-year life of bonds) and compute present-value loss over bond life; mere possibility of interest change is not a bar where probative evidence supports likelihood of damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process baseline: notice and hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions meet due process where opposing parties are afforded notice and a full and fair hearing before being required to post bond, and the bond is payable only if the public agency actually loses (i.e., the opponent ultimately prevails).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases cited (e.g., Buckholts, Asmussen) treat notice and hearing plus the conditional nature of liability (payable only upon opponent's loss) as satisfying due process requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigency considerations and rational-basis test
rubrics_metrics.description: Indigents are not automatically exempt from bond requirements; the test is whether imposition of bond has a rational justification and reasonably furthers a legitimate state interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will uphold bond statutes against indigency claims if alternatives exist (ability to show entitlement to injunction so bond not imposed; ability to appeal; other avenues of relief) and if the requirement is uniformly and nondiscriminatorily applied to further legitimate state interests (e.g., protecting public finances from delay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative purpose: prevent frivolous blockage of bond issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A legislative purpose in enacting the statute was to stop the 'age old practice of allowing one disgruntled taxpayer to stop the entire bond issue by simply filing suit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legitimate state interest (protecting public projects from abusive or meritless litigation-caused delay) underpins constitutionality and rational basis justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on courts retaining jurisdiction after dismissal for failure to post
rubrics_metrics.description: After dismissal for failure to post bond and lapse of the appeal/posting period, no court shall have further jurisdiction of any action to the extent it involves any issue which was or could have been raised in the proceedings (except issues that could have been raised by a party for whom no motion was made).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute operates as preclusive jurisdictional bar over further litigation of those issues unless preserved by appeal or other specified exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond payable only if public agency prevails
rubrics_metrics.description: The bond is payable to the public agency for damages and costs which may accrue 'in the event that the public agency finally prevails and obtains substantially the judgment prayed for in its petition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conditional payoff is emphasized as a protective feature distinguishing the statute from punitive or fee-exacting regimes and as mitigating due-process concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on deciding entire case from partial hearing (Rosenberg principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: A judgment, decision, or determination by a judge or chancellor prior to a hearing of all the evidence amounts to a deprivation of property without due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a court hears only part of the evidence (e.g., only bond-related evidence) and reaches a determination effectively deciding the entire case, there is a due-process concern; courts should not decide the merits solely on partial hearings that determine the entire litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's power to modify interlocutory orders and revisit bond requests
rubrics_metrics.description: An interlocutory order is not res judicata of the issue it addresses; during the pendency of a cause, a trial court retains the power to modify or set aside its interlocutory orders and to enter new orders, whether requested by a party or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public agencies may renew motions for bond; courts may readdress bond requirements as circumstances change.
